title: English discography of his dates; Nellie Lutcher and Goodman sextet sessions
summary: English fans gave Lee a book of his record dates, reminding him of Nellie Lutcher, Dinah Shore and Benny Goodman sessions, and click-track studio work.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: They could tell you every ... some of the questions I could not answer for you, they could answer them in England. They know every record date you have ever played on. As a matter of fact, I have the book someplace, if I go downstairs and try to find it -- but they gave me one. They gave me a little book of every record date I had played on. I'm talking about things I did with Dinah Shore, Nellie Lutcher ... you know.
This is one that has been published? Or one they made up for you?

No, it was published, because they gave me that thing in 1954, the first time we were over there, and I was really amazed, you know, because I had done a lot of recording with different vocalists -- because you know, like "Hurry on Down" and "Brown Frame" and all of those things, I did with Nellie Lutcher.

No, I was a drummer on those things that she did. But they know all about that, you know -- then you'll sit up and you'll forget, you know -- I didn't remember recording with Nellie until someone said, "Hurry on Down", you know.

Yeah, because it's another gig, you know -- it's just another day at the factory, just another recording date. But all kinds of things ... Dinah Shore and Benny Goodman sextet. I did the second "The World Is Waiting for the Sunrise" that he did, Benny did, you know, but I did some nice things with Mel Powell, because those were fun things. I kind of liked to reflect on those things, because I got more enjoyment out of those types of recordings than I did the studio, because the studio was almost like canned music, you know? You got to be -- it's a precision thing, and you look at the picture sometimes, and you have to play from the click track, and I think all drummers hate to play from a click track. But you got to do it to keep the thing in sync.
And it pays better than the other
